title: The Confectioner, His Wife, and the Parrot

keywords: the confectioner his wife and the parrot
full_text:
To illustrate the danger of deceptive appearances, the Second Vizier related the history of a confectioner in Baghdad:

'In the sweetmakers’ quarter lived an honest confectioner who made sesame pastries and pistachio halwa. In his shop he kept a remarkable green parrot gifted with fluent speech, which reported everything that occurred during the master’s absence.

One day, while the confectioner was delivering pastries to a wedding feast, an envious neighbor slipped into the shop and spilled a jar of orange-blossom syrup. When the confectioner returned, the parrot truthfully reported: "The neighbor spilled the syrup!" The confectioner demanded restitution, and the neighbor was shamed before the quarter.

Resolved to destroy the bird’s credibility, the neighbor and his accomplices climbed to the shop roof the following night. They turned a stone handmill to create the sound of thunder, shook mirrors to produce lightning, and poured water through a basket to mimic torrential rain.

All night, the poor parrot was terrified by the artificial tempest.

When the confectioner entered his shop at dawn and asked: "What news of the night?" the parrot answered: "O master, the heavens opened with thunder and lightning, and rain poured in torrents!"

The confectioner stepped outside: the sky was cloudless, the street dust dry as bone, and the sun shining brightly.

Believing the bird was a liar that invented false charges against honest neighbors, the confectioner flew into a rage and silenced the bird forever. Only later, when he found the wet basket and mirrors upon the roof, did he realize that the parrot had spoken only what it experienced, leaving the confectioner to mourn his hasty, tragic folly.'
moral: Truth must not be silenced by deceit; hasty violence against the honest witness brings lifelong regret.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Confectioner His Wife and the Parrot"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
